doc.citation: Fijałkowska-Mader, A. & Malec, J. 2018. Wiek dolnodewońskiego poziomu tufitowego z Barczy (Góry Świętokrzyskie) na podstawie miospor. Przegląd Geologiczny 66(9): 578–584.
doc.language: Polish; English abstract and figure captions
doc.comment: One productive sample among six tested; all 11 illustrated taxa belong to this sample. Regional palynozone summaries concern earlier studies and are not additional taxon-level assemblages. Fijałkowska-Mader and Malec (2011) supplies the regional correlation framework and the section adapted in Figure 6; reuse of its spore specimens is not stated. The tuffite is dated indirectly by spores below it. DOI matches the paper; live Crossref verification was unavailable.

items.section_or_core: Eastern quarry, northern wall, middle part; Figure 3B
items.depth_or_level: Grey-green mudstone below the pyroclastic deposits, approximately 1.7 m above the medium-bedded ferruginous sandstone bed in the upper part of the thick-bedded sandstone complex
items.age_basis_detail: Emphanisporites annulatus indicates the AB (annulatus-bellatulus) palynological zone; Coronaspora mariae places the assemblage in its upper part.
items.setting_as_reported: Grey-green mudstones below pyroclastic deposits, within a mudstone–sandstone complex between medium- and thick-bedded quartzitic sandstones; dispersed plant remains and bioturbation occur in the complex.
items.notes: Relatively rich assemblage described as consisting exclusively of Lower Devonian miospores. Six samples were tested from mudstones below the pyroclastic deposits in the northern and eastern quarries; only this eastern-quarry sample was productive. Figure 3 shows four barren samples in the northern quarry and one in the eastern quarry. No cryptospores are explicitly reported. The authors retain the informal name Barcza Beds because proposed formation/member names require formalisation. The body text prints the genus as 'Calamosora', whereas Figure 5 identifies the illustrated specimen as Calamospora atava. Abundance statements for nondominant taxa apply collectively at genus level.
